The test image shows a close-up of soybean stems/petioles with dark reddish-brown to dark brown elongated lesions near a node. Green pods are visible. No white mold, no powdery coating, no leaf symptoms. Key features: elongated dark brown lesions on stem/petiole tissue at a node.

Top candidates: Anthracnose (brown irregular spots on stems/petioles), Cercospora (reddish-purple on petioles/stems), Phytophthora (dark brown stem).

The Anthracnose reference shows dried pods with dark acervuli on tan tissue — quite different from the test image which shows **elongated dark reddish-brown lesions on green petiole/stem tissue near a node**, with the plant still actively growing and green pods present.

Comparing to symptom descriptions:
- **Cercospora**: "reddish-purple lesions on petioles, stems, and pods" — matches the dark reddish-brown elongated discoloration on the petiole
- **Anthracnose**: darker acervuli/pin-cushion structures on dying/dried tissue — doesn't match the still-green context
- **Phytophthora**: chocolate-brown from soil line upward — wrong location

The dark reddish-brown/purplish elongated lesion along the petiole at a node on an otherwise green, actively growing plant is most consistent with Cercospora blight affecting the petiole tissue.
